findings.obligation: L7 and T1: the sentence that refuses a project key has exactly one home, witnessed by the gate refusing a planted second copy
findings.observation: The planted file carries four wordings of the sentence at once (project/Project, A to Z/A-Z) and the Then step needs only a non-zero exit and the file name, so any gate clause that bites one of the four passes. A clause whose needle is a wording the product does not ship (for example A-Z while the refusal Display reads A to Z) passes this scenario while a second copy of the sentence the product really ships stays unguarded; the mirror case, a needle carrying an article or a full stop that matches none of the four, fails a correct gate and so couples the oracle to the crafter copy choice the design leaves open. The measured RED (gate exit Some(0) on all three areas, scratchpad/run3.txt) is sound, so the obligation does have a falsifier; only its strength is reduced.
findings.remediation: Derive the planted text at run time from the shipped refusal (foundry-acceptance already depends on foundry-core at Cargo.toml:30, so the Display of a refused ProjectKey gives the exact sentence) and plant that one text, one plant per Examples row; keep the extra wordings only as further rows if drift between them is also to be guarded. This keeps the law independent of the wording the crafter picks and is constructible now, before craft.
